search_log: Searched: "Small Things Like These" Claire Keegan excerpt publisher.
Searched: "Small Things Like These" "third person" narrator.
Searched Grove Atlantic and Faber domains for an authorized excerpt; the publisher pages primarily supplied catalog material, while the Booker-hosted Faber extract supplied sustained opening prose.
Opened and assessed the Booker Prize extract, the publisher-authorized Oprah Daily/Grove Press excerpt, GradeSaver's narrator description, and LitCharts' narrator analysis.
Searched for epistolary, frame-narrative, multiple-narrator, and alternating-point-of-view evidence; found no credible indication of a person shift or participating narrator.
A scholarly article on the novella's historical intervention was opened but did not provide a sufficiently explicit person or whole-book narrator statement, so it was not used as supporting evidence.
person_note: The controlling narration is close third person centered on Bill Furlong. Numerous Goodreads passages sustain external he/Furlong reference while entering his memories, perceptions, knowledge, and free-indirect thoughts; dialogue, maxims, paratext, and clipped fragments were not allowed to vote as base narration. Independent authorized opening and interior excerpts show the same third-person method, and two whole-book guides explicitly identify close or limited third person. No source indicated a first-person frame, second-person strand, epistolary structure, or alternating-person section. The main limitation is that the Tier A excerpts do not reproduce the entire novella, but their agreement with the distributed quote evidence and explicit whole-book descriptions supports high confidence.
